h1: API 570 Training: Self-Paced Exam Preparation for the Piping Inspector Certification
html:
API 570 training for the piping inspector examination

API 570 certification is the credential refineries, chemical plants and inspection contractors look for in the people who plan and carry out in-service inspection of process piping. The examination behind it is set by the American Petroleum Institute, which also decides each candidate's eligibility and issues the certificate. You sit it in person at a Prometric centre: 170 questions over a 7.5-hour day, 110 of them closed-book in 2.75 hours and 60 open-book in 3.75 hours after a 45-minute lunch, with only 140 of the 170 counting toward your result.

The Atlantis NDT API 570 course prepares you for that examination. You study online at your own pace, from the day you enrol to the window you book, and an instructor answers your questions as you meet them. The course does not stand between you and API: the application, the eligibility decision, the exam and the certificate all stay with API.

Who takes API 570, and the eligibility rules in brief

The typical API 570 candidate has spent years around piping already: an ultrasonic thickness technician who has logged readings at thousands of condition monitoring locations, a pipefitter or welder who moved into QA/QC, an operator who joined the inspection department, or a reliability engineer who approves piping inspection plans. Some sit API 570 as their opening API certification; others add it to API 510 or API 653 because owner-users often want one inspector who can cover the vessels, tanks and the piping between them.

Eligibility is decided by API on education plus experience with in-service metallic piping, gained within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract to, an authorized inspection agency. With an engineering or technology degree you need one year supervising or performing inspection. A two-year degree or certificate calls for two years of piping experience including one in inspection; a high school diploma calls for three, again with one in inspection; and with no formal education the requirement is five years or more. The API 570 certification requirements page sets out the detail, including how technical military service counts; the course assumes you have checked it before you start.

What is on the API 570 exam: the publications and their editions

Each set of API 570 windows has its own Body of Knowledge and Publications Effectivity Sheet. When this page was written, the effectivity sheet API had published for its upcoming API 570 windows listed the editions below. Always download the sheet for the window you book, because editions change and the exam follows the sheet, not the newest copy on the shelf.

PublicationEdition on the sheetScope examined
API 5705th edition, 2024Entire code
API RP 5713rd edition, 2020Definitions and 15 listed damage mechanisms only
API RP 5745th edition, 2024, with Addendum 1 (2025)Entire document
API RP 5765th edition, 2024Sections 5, 6.1 to 6.5 and 7
API RP 5773rd edition, 2020Entire document
API RP 5784th edition, 2023Entire document
ASME B31.32024 editionSelected paragraphs; many sections excluded
ASME B16.52020 editionRatings, materials, dimensions, marking and testing
ASME Section V2023 editionArticles 1, 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10, and SE-797 in Article 23
ASME Section IX2023 editionWelding only
ASME PCC-22022 editionTwelve listed repair and testing articles

The B31.3 exclusions matter as much as the inclusions. Branch reinforcement, most of the design chapter beyond straight pipe and blanks, the flexibility-analysis paragraphs and several chapters and appendices are outside the Body of Knowledge, so the course concentrates your B31.3 time on what is examined: quality factors, pressure design thickness, blanks, materials and impact testing, fabrication, preheat and heat treatment, examination and leak testing. The RP 571 list is the set of mechanisms piping inspectors meet most, among them amine and caustic cracking, chloride stress corrosion cracking, corrosion under insulation, erosion-corrosion, galvanic, hydrochloric acid and sour water corrosion, vibration-induced fatigue, microbiologically influenced corrosion, soil corrosion and sulfidation. The ASME B31.3 explainer and the API 570 code explainer are useful background reading.

API 570 calculations, worked through

The Body of Knowledge names the API 570 calculations precisely: corrosion rate, remaining life and inspection interval from API 570; casting and weld joint quality factors, the pressure design thickness of straight pipe and blank thickness from B31.3; the MAWP of corroded pipe; hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressure; impact-test exemption and Charpy values; preheat and heat treatment; thermal expansion; and flange pressure-temperature ratings from B16.5. Here is how the main ones work, with round numbers that carry from one example to the next.

Pressure design thickness of straight pipe (B31.3, 304.1.2)

For NPS 6 pipe the outside diameter D is 6.625 in. Take a design pressure P of 600 psi, an allowable stress S of 20,000 psi as given in the problem, a quality factor E of 1.0 for seamless pipe, a weld joint strength reduction factor W of 1.0, and the coefficient Y of 0.4 that Table 304.1.1 gives for ferritic steels up to 900°F.

  • t = PD ÷ 2(SEW + PY) = (600 × 6.625) ÷ 2(20,000 + 240) = 3,975 ÷ 40,480 = 0.098 in.
  • The minimum required thickness tm adds the mechanical, corrosion and erosion allowance c to that figure.

In service, readings are usually judged against the greater of the pressure design thickness and a structural minimum, because a thin small-bore line can satisfy pressure long after it has stopped being able to carry its own weight and the loads on it. RP 574 discusses structural minimums, and owner-users usually set their own. Switch to electric-resistance-welded pipe and E drops to 0.85 from Table A-1B, which raises the required thickness; taking the wrong quality factor is among the commonest errors on this question.

Corrosion rate, remaining life and the interval by piping class

At one condition monitoring location (CML) on that line, the baseline reading was 0.275 in. 12 years ago, the previous reading 0.230 in. four years ago, and today's reading is 0.205 in. The owner's structural minimum for the line, 0.110 in., is greater than the 0.098 in. pressure design thickness, so it governs.

  • Long-term rate = (0.275 − 0.205) ÷ 12 = 0.0058 in. per year.
  • Short-term rate = (0.230 − 0.205) ÷ 4 = 0.00625 in. per year, the higher of the two.
  • Remaining life = (0.205 − 0.110) ÷ 0.00625 = 15.2 years.
  • Thickness measurement interval = the lesser of half the remaining life and the maximum for the piping class in API 570 Table 1. Half the life is 7.6 years. A Class 2 line has a 10-year maximum, so its interval is 7.6 years; on a Class 1 line the 5-year maximum governs; Class 3 also has a 10-year maximum.

External visual inspection carries its own maximums by class, 5 years for Classes 1 and 2 and 10 years for Class 3, and the table has separate rows for injection points and soil-to-air interfaces. Questions often hide the class inside a description of the fluid, so learn the class definitions as well as the numbers. The guides to API 570 piping service classes and to long-term and short-term corrosion rates go further.

MAWP of corroded pipe (API 570, 7.5)

To set the pressure a corroded line can keep running at until its next inspection, API 570 has you subtract twice the corrosion expected before that inspection from the measured thickness, then put the result into the B31.3 formula rearranged for pressure, P = 2SEWt ÷ (D − 2Yt). With today's 0.205 in., the short-term rate of 0.00625 in. per year and the next inspection in 5 years, the expected loss is 0.03125 in. and the thickness used is 0.205 − 2 × 0.03125 = 0.1425 in. Then P = (2 × 20,000 × 0.1425) ÷ (6.625 − 0.8 × 0.1425) = 5,700 ÷ 6.511 = about 875 psi. The pipe wall is not the limit at 600 psi, so the next thing to check is the flanges and valves.

Flange ratings and the most economical flange (B16.5)

B16.5 questions ask for a flange's maximum working pressure at a temperature, the maximum temperature at a pressure, or the lowest pressure class that will do the job. Find the material group in Table 1.1-1 (forged A105 carbon steel, for example, is Group 1.1), then read that group's rating table. In the 2020 edition, Group 1.1 flanges are rated 285 psig for Class 150 and 740 psig for Class 300 from −20°F to 100°F. A line at 600 psig and 100°F therefore needs Class 300, because Class 150 falls far short. Ratings fall as temperature rises and you may interpolate between table temperatures, so a hotter line can push you up a class.

Hydrostatic and pneumatic leak test pressure (B31.3, 345)

The minimum hydrostatic test pressure is PT = 1.5 × P × Rr, where Rr is the ratio of allowable stress at test temperature to allowable stress at design temperature, capped at 6.5. For the 600 psi line, if S is 20,000 psi at the test temperature and 18,000 psi at a hot design temperature, Rr = 1.11 and PT = 1.5 × 600 × 1.11 = 1,000 psi. A pneumatic test is set at 1.1 times design pressure, 660 psi here, and needs extra safeguards because of the energy stored in compressed gas. Either way the pressure is held for at least 10 minutes before the leak examination, and where the hydrostatic test pressure would stress the pipe beyond yield, B31.3 allows it to be reduced, a detail exam questions like to probe.

Impact testing, blanks, heat treatment and thermal expansion

Low-temperature questions use Figure 323.2.2A: you place the carbon steel on its curve, read the lowest temperature it may see without impact testing at its thickness, and decide whether tests are needed; Table 323.3.5 then gives the Charpy values those tests must reach. Blank thickness under 304.5.3 is worked from the inside diameter of the gasket rather than the pipe diameter, a detail candidates forget. Preheat comes from Table 330.1.1 by P-Number and thickness, and heat-treatment questions follow paragraph 331. Thermal expansion questions read Table C-1, which gives the total expansion in inches per 100 ft between 70°F and the stated temperature: if the table gives 1.8 in. per 100 ft, a 250 ft run grows 2.5 × 1.8 = 4.5 in.

Beyond the numbers: CMLs, circuits and inspection planning

A large share of API 570 questions are not calculations at all. They test whether you can plan the inspection of a piping system the way the code intends: dividing it into circuits of similar material and service, choosing and numbering condition monitoring locations where damage is likely, deciding when thickness readings alone are not enough, and recognising the places that corrode differently from the rest of the line. The course works through each with RP 574 open alongside the code:

  • CML selection and density: more locations where corrosion is localised or the consequence of a leak is high, fewer on a line with slow, uniform loss, and readings taken at the same spot every time so that the rates mean something.
  • Injection and mix points: treated as circuits in their own right, with closer attention upstream and downstream (see injection point inspection).
  • Deadlegs: stagnant branches where corrosion can run much faster than in the active line (see deadleg inspection).
  • Corrosion under insulation: the temperature ranges and locations most at risk, and how to target them (see CUI in inspection plans).
  • Soil-to-air interfaces, small-bore and auxiliary piping, and buried piping: each has its own expectations in the code.
  • Repairs, alterations and rerating: what needs the inspector's authorisation, what welding and testing follow, and how temporary repairs are treated.

Welding, PWHT and NDE questions on the API 570 exam

API 570 candidates meet welding in three places. Section IX questions hand you a WPS and PQR, or a welder's qualification record, and ask whether they comply: the essential variables, the test results and whether the welder is qualified for what the procedure allows. The exam limits this to one process per document (SMAW, GTAW, GMAW or SAW) and to P-No. 1, 3, 4, 5 and 8 base metals, and it states the transformation temperatures you should use. RP 577 covers welding processes, welding inspection and metallurgy in full. And B31.3 questions on fabrication and examination ask about preheat, heat treatment, the extent of examination and leak testing. If procedure qualification is new to you, read the guide to WPS, PQR and WPQ early on.

On the NDE side, the API 570 list of Section V articles is wider than the API 510 list: visual examination (Article 9) and leak testing (Article 10) join the general requirements, radiography, liquid penetrant, magnetic particle by yoke and prod, and SE-797 ultrasonic thickness measurement. Expect questions on what a compliant procedure must contain and how an examination is carried out, rather than on interpreting indications.

Is the API 570 exam open book? Working the B31.3 PDF

Only the last 60 questions are open-book, and the reference material is the set of PDFs the test centre provides, so nothing you have marked up comes in with you. That makes code navigation a skill to practise, not something to leave to the day. B31.3 is long, and the open-book questions often come from its tables: Table A-1 allowable stresses, Table A-1B quality factors, Table 323.3.5 impact values, Table 330.1.1 preheat, and the B16.5 rating tables. Know the table numbers by heart so you can go straight to them, and read the notes under each table, because questions turn on them. If one question is eating your time, flag it and move on; the 60 open-book questions share 3.75 hours.

The closed-book half is the other side of the coin. The corrosion rate, remaining life and MAWP formulas, the class intervals, the definitions and the inspection practices from RP 574 all have to come from memory. The timed papers in the course copy both halves so you practise switching from recall to look-up and back.

How to pass the API 570 exam: a study sequence

  1. Start with the documents. Get the Body of Knowledge and effectivity sheet for your window and the exact editions they name.
  2. API 570 cover to cover. It is examined in full, and its definitions, inspection types, intervals, CML rules, repairs and rerating carry most of the closed-book marks.
  3. RP 574 alongside it. Read the recommended practice as the explanation of the code: piping components, deterioration, inspection methods and records.
  4. The calculation set. Thickness, corrosion rate, remaining life, interval, MAWP, test pressure, flange rating, blanks and expansion, in US and SI units, until they are automatic.
  5. B31.3 navigation. Learn where each examined paragraph and table lives, and which ones are excluded.
  6. Damage mechanisms and welding. The 15 RP 571 mechanisms, RP 577, Section IX document review and the PCC-2 articles.
  7. Full timed papers. Closed-book then open-book, to time, with every wrong answer traced back to the paragraph it came from.

There is no fixed time this takes; it depends on how much of the material you already use at work. The sign that you are ready is steady scores on full timed papers, not the number of pages you have read. Free questions to use with the course are on the API 570 practice questions page.

API 570 online exam prep: what to look for in a course

Search for API 570 preparation and you will find intensive seminars timed before each window, blended programmes, recorded video lessons and large question banks. They differ less in content than in how they fit around your work. A piping inspector on a rotating schedule, or a technician who cannot be released for a week before a turnaround, usually gets more from material they can return to than from a seminar they have to attend in one block.

Whichever you choose, check that it names the editions on your effectivity sheet, teaches the B31.3 and API 570 calculations step by step, lets you ask a person when you are stuck, and gives you practice papers with the real closed-book and open-book split. Be careful with question banks advertised as real exam questions: API's examinations are confidential, and answers taken from an older edition of B31.3 or API 570 can be wrong for your window. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider; the course is independent preparation, and certification comes only from passing API's examination.

Sponsoring API 570 candidates, and what comes after the exam

Owner-users and inspection contractors often enrol several piping inspectors together, for example to meet a contract that names API 570 inspectors or to build cover before a turnaround. Because the course is self-paced, a senior UT technician and a newly qualified engineer can enrol together and each move at the speed their background allows. Each candidate must still meet API's rules and apply to API individually. Fees are quoted on request for one candidate or a group.

After a pass, the API 570 Piping Inspector certification runs for three years. To recertify, you show that at least 20% of your time over the last three years went on piping inspection, log 24 hours of continuing professional development in at least two categories, and every six years complete a 25-question open-book web quiz on code changes; miss the 90-day grace period after expiry and you must apply afresh and sit the full exam. For teams building wider capability, Atlantis also runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based UT Level II training for the technicians who take the thickness readings, the AWS CWI exam-prep course for welding inspectors, and remote risk-based inspection studies for owners who want piping intervals set by risk.

faq.q: Is the API 570 exam open book?
faq.a: Only partly. Of the 170 questions, 110 are closed-book and answered from memory in 2.75 hours. The remaining 60 are open-book: the examined publications, including B31.3 and B16.5, are on screen as PDFs for 3.75 hours. You cannot take your own copies, notes or tabs into the Prometric centre, so practise finding tables and paragraphs in plain PDFs before exam day.

faq.q: What calculations are on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Corrosion rate, remaining life and the inspection interval by piping class from API 570; casting and weld joint quality factors, straight-pipe pressure design thickness and blank thickness from B31.3; the MAWP of corroded pipe; hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressure; impact-test exemption temperatures and Charpy values; preheat and heat treatment; thermal expansion from Table C-1; and flange working pressure and class selection from B16.5. Branch reinforcement is excluded.

faq.q: Can I prepare for API 570 online?
faq.a: Yes. The Atlantis course is self-paced and online: you begin when you enrol, fit study around your shifts, and an instructor answers your questions on calculations, code paragraphs and open-book searches. The examination is a separate step. You apply to API, and API holds the exam in person at Prometric test centres during its set windows; see the API exam windows and deadlines.

faq.q: Which B31.3 edition is on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: The one named on the Publications Effectivity Sheet for your exam window. When this page was written, the sheet API had published for its upcoming API 570 windows listed the 2024 edition of B31.3, alongside the 5th edition of API 570 and the 2020 edition of B16.5. Editions change between windows, so download the sheet for the window you book and study that edition.

faq.q: Should I take API 510 or API 570 first?
faq.a: It depends on the equipment you work on and what your employer or clients ask for. Piping is a large share of the inspection workload at most refineries and chemical plants, so many inspectors start with API 570; others start with API 510 because their work is mainly vessels and exchangers. The two Bodies of Knowledge share RP 571, RP 576, RP 577, RP 578, Section V, Section IX and PCC-2, though not always the same sections, which shortens the second one. See which API certification to take first.

faq.q: Do I have to be an NDT technician to take API 570?
faq.a: No. API looks at education and in-service piping experience gained in the last 10 years with an authorized inspection agency, with at least one year supervising or performing inspection. NDT technicians are common candidates, but welders, pipefitters in QA/QC, operators and engineers qualify through the same routes. No NDT certification is part of the requirement; the API 570 certification page has the full rules.

faq.q: Is the Atlantis API 570 course approved by API?
faq.a: No. Atlantis NDT is not an API-approved, API-accredited or API-endorsed training provider. The course is independent exam preparation built on the Body of Knowledge and effectivity sheet API publishes. API decides eligibility, administers the examination and issues the API 570 certification; completing a course, ours or anyone else's, does not certify you.

faq.q: Can an employer enrol a group of API 570 candidates?
faq.a: Yes. Inspection contractors and owner-users regularly sponsor several candidates at once. Each person starts when they enrol and works at their own pace, and each applies to API separately, since eligibility is assessed individually. Send the number of candidates and the windows they are aiming for through the enquiry link on this page and we reply with the course details and a quote.
